Hi Simon — thanks for the heads up. Looping in Laura (billing) and Neha (payments ops) to confirm the cleanest path. Quick answers up front:

- We can accept a single EUR payment into our EUR nostro and perform the USD payout/FX on our side if you prefer a single movement. We can also accept two legs (EUR + USD) if your treasury prefers to net locally.
- Intermediary bank fees: Redwood does not currently re-invoice individual correspondent fees back to customers; by default those are deducted in transit (BEN) unless we explicitly request OUR (sender pays) or the sender covers with an additional add-on. For EU VAT treatment, intermediary fees are typically outside Redwood's invoiced goods/services line and so they are not VAT-able on our invoice by default.

We should decide whether Redwood will:
  a) ask the sender to use OUR (sender covers all correspondent charges), or
  b) accept BEN and Redwood absorbs the variability up to a threshold, or
  c) accept BEN and have Globex top up to cover the shortfall.

Laura / Neha — can you review and I'll propose a single approach and a wire template.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee

> Laura / Neha — can you review and I'll propose a single approach and a wire template.

Thanks — quick notes from Billing:

- VAT: For EU customers where we issue an invoice to an EU-registered business with a valid VAT number, we apply reverse-charge (no VAT on Redwood invoice) for software services. Correspondent bank fees are services charged by the bank and not by Redwood; we do not list them as line items on our standard invoice. If Globex needs a VATable invoice that includes bank fees for their reclaim, we can issue a Supplementary Invoice but we'd need a clear reconciliation (bank statement or intermediary fee receipt) to avoid misstatement.

- FX handling: If we accept EUR and convert to pay out USD to Redwood's USD account, we will apply our internal FX margin. If customer prefers to avoid Redwood FX margin, they can route a separate USD leg.

Attached a proposed_wire_template.xlsx with the exact fields we need (beneficiary, account, SWIFT, interbank instructions, routing code, remittance reference).

- Recommendation: Ask sender to use OUR for the EUR leg where possible. If sender insists on BEN, Redwood will absorb up to $25 per inbound wire for intermediary deductions and will reconcile monthly. Anything above that we will request to be billed/credited on the following month.

Laura Bennett

Simon — attaching the wire template Laura prepared. Summary of the proposed approach:

1) Preferred: Globex instructs their bank to send an OUR EUR wire to our EUR nostro (so sender covers correspondent costs). This prevents deductions in transit and is the simplest for reconciling net amounts.

2) If the sender cannot use OUR: Globex may send a BEN EUR wire to the same account. Redwood will absorb intermediary/correspondent deductions up to $25 per inbound wire and will reconcile any excess >$25 monthly (we can either deduct from future invoices or issue a credit).

3) VAT: For EU-registered Globex entities with a valid VAT ID we will issue a reverse-charge invoice (no VAT). If you require bank fees to be part of the VAT reclaim, send us the intermediary fee receipts (from your bank) and we will issue a supplementary invoice listing the fees so your tax team has documentation — this is an exceptional workflow and requires reconciliation.

4) FX: If you want Redwood to convert EUR -> USD for our internal settlement, we will apply our published FX spread. If you'd like to avoid that spread, please route a separate USD wire to our USD account.

Please confirm which of the above you prefer and we'll mark the invoice and wire instructions accordingly. Template attached.

Thanks,
Soojin

(Attachment: proposed_wire_template.xlsx)

Those fees are charged by the intermediary and deducted from the beneficiary unless the instructing bank sets the charges=OUR field. We cannot retroactively recover deductions once the payment is processed.
